summary: Verified independently: all 8 applicable XP boxes (.110 .123 .124 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240) were in ONE Tribes 2 CTF game on tribes2-lan at the same time. The server roster names all 8 Fleet<octet> players. Each box sent 129-150 packets per 10 s to :28001. Every frame shows the box spawned with the HUD up. .186 (no 3D driver on Win7) and .243 (P166, gated) are NA. The game was then closed gracefully on all 8 boxes, and no tribes2.exe process remains.
issues: .124 auto-updated its agent 1.98.0 -> 1.100.1 in the middle of the first check. Its agent console took the foreground, the fbshot caught the desktop, and 9898/9897 refused for a short time. The game kept sending packets. Once the agent was back, Tribes 2 had the foreground again, and a re-check plus fbshot (Tribes2_124_final.jpg) showed it in-game. The box did not reboot (uptime 6.4 h).

.240 raised a modal 'Color Depth' dialog on launch ('To run in 16 bit color, you must set your desktop to 16 bit color. Continue in 32 bit color?'). It needed one RETURN before the box connected. To make the join unattended, the staged ClientPrefs should preset 32-bit.
Every box loads in observer mode and needs one FIRE click to spawn (.171 needed three). Not a blocker for joining.
The main tribes2-server on :28000 runs -online with TribesNext auth, and no box can join it unattended. Only the -nologin tribes2-lan instance on :28001 works for the fleet.
After the close, all 8 boxes are back at their desktops in normal modes (110 1600x1200, 123/124/133/143/171 1280x1024, 184 1024x768, 240 1920x1080). No crash dialogs.
library_fix_needed: Tribes2: preset 32-bit colour depth in the staged client prefs so the 'Color Depth' modal never blocks the join (seen on .240).
